correctness.rationale: The Euler-product identity holds for every square input. Exact rational seven-case certificates and Defant 2015 Lemma 2.2 prove the global tail inequalities, not merely finite observations. The binary-subsums lemma is reconstructed; local-interval overlap and exact disjointness are fully proved. verify.py checks all finite exceptional comparisons and 60000 independent integer cases. Limits: source prime-gap lemma and Euler evaluation are cited rather than reproved.

value.rationale: A complete topological classification on the natural perfect-square subdomain reveals four components, not three as in the unrestricted reciprocal-square divisor function. A fourth interval and exact boundaries are not automatically inherited from the unrestricted theorem. This offers a precise object and exact invariant useful for studying additive arithmetic functions on square inputs. No arbitrary finite cutoff is used.
